provenance: The county records, resolved locations and national base rates of the data pack the backtest verdicts were recorded on, extracted by tests/backtest.rs (RR_WRITE_BACKTEST=1). Not the data pack: a frozen copy so the verdicts do not move with each refresh (docs/VALIDATION.md).

outages.event_definition: EAGLE-I outage event: starts when at least 1% of the county's electricity customers (the larger of ORNL's modelled customer count and the county's households; at least 10 customers) are reported without power, needs at least 1 hour at that level, and lasts until fewer than 0.25% (at least 5) remain out, with dips or missing 15-minute snapshots of up to 2 hours bridged. Short reversals inside an event (under half of the current peak or trough, or under the 1% level) are treated as reporting noise. Durations are per customer: customers are assumed to be restored in the order they lost power. Rates are customer outages in such events per customer per year of data.

base_rates.note: 131,434 thousand households in 2023 (Table HH-1, 2023 row). Denominator for household rates.

base_rates.unit: residential building fires per household per year
base_rates.note: 344,600 residential building fires in 2023 (344,600 fires / 131,434,000 households). About 1 in 381 households a year. Counts fires reported to fire departments.

base_rates.unit: residential fire deaths per household per year
base_rates.note: 2,890 residential fire deaths in 2023 (2,890 deaths / 131,434,000 households).

base_rates.unit: residential fire injuries per household per year
base_rates.note: 10,400 residential fire injuries in 2023 (10,400 injuries / 131,434,000 households).

base_rates.unit: US dollars of direct loss per residential building fire
base_rates.note: $11.27 billion direct loss from 344,600 residential building fires in 2023 ($11,270,000,000 / 344,600 fires). A mean; most fires cost far less and a few cost far more.

base_rates.unit: layoffs and discharges per worker per month
base_rates.note: 2025 average of the 12 monthly rates: 1.1167% (mean of monthly JTS000000000000000LDR values / 100). Counts events, not people: some workers are laid off twice, so per-person risk is lower.

base_rates.unit: chance of at least one layoff or discharge per worker per year (upper bound)
base_rates.note: 1.1167% a month (1 - (1 - monthly rate)^12). An upper bound: layoffs cluster in high-turnover jobs, so a typical worker's chance is lower.

base_rates.unit: chance a labour-force participant is unemployed at some point in a year
base_rates.note: work-experience unemployment rate 8.3% in 2024 (14.7 million people unemployed at some time during the year) (8.3 / 100). People unemployed at some point in the year / people who worked or looked for work; includes people who quit or were entering the labour force, so it overstates involuntary job loss.

base_rates.unit: emergency department visits per person per year
share of emergency department visits that lead to hospital admission
base_rates.note: 11.5% of visits resulted in hospital admission (2022) (11.5 / 100).

base_rates.unit: injury-related emergency department visits per person per year
base_rates.note: 43.5 million injury-related visits of 155.4 million (2022) (0.473 x 43.5 / 155.4).

base_rates.unit: unintentional-injury deaths per person per year
traffic deaths per 100 million vehicle miles traveled
base_rates.note: 36,640 deaths (early estimate); 1.10 fatalities per 100 million VMT (2025) (as published). All road deaths per mile driven, not only vehicle occupants.

base_rates.unit: people injured in traffic crashes per person per year
base_rates.note: 2.44 million people injured (2023); U.S. population 336755052 (Census Vintage 2025, July 1, 2023) (2,440,000 / population 2023).

base_rates.unit: chance a new pandemic begins in a given year
base_rates.note: 5 pandemic onsets in 108 years (1918, 1957, 1968, 2009, 2020; 1918-2025) (1 - exp(-5/108); range is the exact Poisson 90% interval for 5 events). A crude historical rate with wide uncertainty; treat as a planning figure, not a forecast.

base_rates.unit: hours without power per electricity customer per year (national average)
base_rates.note: about 9 hours from major events plus about 2 hours from other events in 2024; major events averaged about 4 hours a year in 2014-2023 (9 + 2; low = 4 + 2 (2014-2023 typical year)). National average; use outages.csv for county detail.
